title: Forecasting Malaria Incidence in Rwanda with Neural CDEs
summary: Doctoral research: continuous-time deep learning for irregularly sampled malaria data, integrated with optimal control tools for intervention planning.
description: My PhD project at the University of Łódź (2025–2029), supervised by Prof. dr hab. Andrzej Nowakowski with Dr hab. D. Machowska as secondary supervisor. The goal is a forecaster that handles the irregular sampling of real epidemiological data and can be coupled to optimal control to recommend intervention schedules for national malaria programmes. A Neural Controlled Differential Equation forecaster is currently under development on top of an established benchmark.
highlights: Rolling-origin forecasting benchmark (naive, ETS, AR, pooled ridge) as the baseline for the Neural CDE forecaster
Data access granted by the DHS Program (Rwanda DHS 2014–15, 2019–20; MIS 2013, 2017, 2023)
Surveillance data request in progress with the Rwanda Biomedical Centre
Presented at the XXXI National Conference on Applications of Mathematics in Biology and Medicine, Kościelisko, Sept 2026

title: SEIRS–SEI Transmission Model with Optimal Control
summary: A calibrated human–mosquito malaria transmission model with ITN, IRS and treatment controls, solved for optimal intervention schedules.
description: Implemented and calibrated a compartmental SEIRS–SEI human–mosquito transmission model for Rwanda with three intervention controls: insecticide-treated nets (ITN), indoor residual spraying (IRS) and treatment. The model reaches a national fit error of 4.2 %. Optimal intervention schedules are derived by direct transcription of the optimal control problem.
highlights: Three intervention controls: ITN, IRS and treatment
Mechanistic baseline for the hybrid Neural CDE approach

title: Rwanda Malaria Analysis Dataset (2000–2022)
summary: A reproducible Python pipeline building a 30-district, 23-year dataset from Malaria Atlas Project surfaces, DHS/MIS surveys and public climate data.
description: The data foundation of the doctoral project. Combines Malaria Atlas Project raster surfaces, survey-weighted DHS and MIS indicators, and public climate data into a district-level panel covering all 30 Rwandan districts from 2000 to 2022. Everything is rebuilt from source by a reproducible pipeline under version control.
highlights: Raster and vector processing in R (malariaAtlas, sf, terra) and Python

title: Legal Connect System Management
summary: MSc thesis project (first class): a system for managing legal services and client–lawyer connections.
description: Master's thesis at the Faculty of Mathematics and Computer Science, University of Łódź, completed with a first-class MSc in Computer Science. The project covered the design and implementation of a management system connecting clients with legal services.
highlights: MSc in Computer Science, First Class (2024)
Completed alongside software-development workshops and professional-certification study groups

title: Order-to-Cash Analytics & Reporting
summary: Credit and cash-collection analytics for a multinational client at Infosys BPM: dashboards, automation and process-improvement analysis on large financial datasets.
description: As Process Specialist (and previously Senior Process Executive) at Infosys BPM Poland, I lead credit and cash-collection analytics for a multinational client. The work includes building reporting dashboards, automating recurring reports and producing process-improvement analyses over large financial datasets in Order-to-Cash and Procure-to-Pay processes.
highlights: Reporting dashboards on large financial datasets
Process-improvement analyses for O2C and P2P
